target.variable: First-release core CPI-U seasonally adjusted monthly percent change
target.instrument_or_population: U.S. city average, all urban consumers
target.outcome_description: October2026 first-release CPI-U all items less food and energy, SA percent change from preceding month, as displayed to one decimal in Table A. The reference month is October; the later deadline is a resolution limit, not the measurement period.
target.timezone_note: Reference month encoded in UTC for metadata, not a measurement instant. For later resolution use2026-10-31T23:59:59Z as an explicitly labeled reference-period endpoint; actual publication/retrieval remain separate. Scheduled08:30America/New_York is13:30UTC on November10.

forecast.horizon: Issue 24 to 72 hours before the captured scheduled release; retain measured lead separately

resolution_rule.dataset_or_instrument: CPI news release Table A: U.S. city average CPI-U, all items less food and energy
resolution_rule.field_or_price_convention: Seasonally adjusted percent change from preceding month, exact one-decimal displayed first-release value
resolution_rule.rule: Resolve to the exact one-decimal core CPI-U monthly percent change in the first official release for the target reference month. Establish the initial vintage from preserved release evidence. Do not replace it with an annual seasonal revision or later correction; show corrections separately. If the initial vintage cannot be established or the release arrives after the declared deadline, leave the primary case unresolved or unverified.
resolution_rule.missing_or_holiday_policy: Retain unissued and missing cases. Do not impute an outcome. Keep the original calendar cutoff and deadline after a delay; report the changed lead and any deadline breach. Never substitute a scheduled release time for actual publication evidence.

comparator.description: Captured Cleveland Fed core CPI monthly model nowcast for the same reference month
comparator.limitations: Public model baseline, not consensus or an independent measurement. Uses lagged core CPI and special substituted2025 inputs; captured table is rounded to two decimals.

forecast.rationale: A fixed50/50 blend reweights the recent archived monthly core print(0.3) relative to the Cleveland smoothed estimate(0.21). Equal weights are a transparent unvalidated candidate, not an empirically selected optimum. Actual lead at issuance is47.291326hours to the captured schedule. Cleveland is the primary benchmark; latest-print persistence is a predeclared secondary check.
forecast.disconfirming_evidence: The 12-month core model could appropriately smooth transient monthly noise, making the overweighted latest print worse. Inputs overlap, substituted historical inputs affect model construction, and rounded first-release outcomes add discretization. A single resolved case cannot establish comparative skill; retain every intended case and all losses.
